narrative:
Skies turn mostly cloudy for your Halloween. While cooler than Friday, temperatures will still be running a bit above normal for the end of October. Oh, and don’t forget to turn those clocks back tonight. Sunday will be generally gray and seasonable, but dry. We may have a bit of spotty light rain and drizzle Sunday night but it won’t amount to much. Sunshine returns by Monday afternoon, with Tuesday perhaps the pick of the week before some rainfall returns toward midweek.

Forecast Discussion

Considerable upper level energy traversing the region today will keep a lot of high cloudiness around the mountains, however a sprawling surface high pressure centered from Buffalo, NY to Washington, DC will keep the weather dry and tranquil.

Really the only possible rainfall over the weekend will be some spotty light rain and drizzle Sunday night. 

Monday should be nice after early cloudiness exits. Tuesday will feature ample sunshine and pleasantly mild temperatures.

Wedging high pressure will meet with an advancing frontal zone by midweek, passing through here on Thursday. That represents our next opportunity for meaningful rainfall, beginning as spotty light rain and/or drizzle on Wednesday, increasing for Wednesday night into at least a portion of Thursday.
